Three-part names (Database.dbo.Table) are allowed and are the way to join across catalogs; four-part names are refused. Pass `databases` to run the same statement across several catalogs (e.g. one per tenant) and get results labelled per catalog.

databases.description: Run against each of these catalogs and label the results per catalog. Mutually exclusive with `database`.

environment.description: Configured environment name. Defaults to the configured default environment.

maxRows.description: Row cap. Reaching it cancels the request, so a batch returning several recordsets is cut off at that point — `truncated: true` says so.

tools.description: Commit a SQL Server write batch previewed by write_preview, using its previewId + approvalToken. Re-runs the exact previewed batch against the previewed environment and catalog, re-checks every gate, and rolls back instead of committing if rowsAffected differs from the preview. Single-use; no rollback tool exists, so read the preview first.
tools.name: write_apply
tools.title: Apply write batch

tools.description: Insert, update or delete SQL Server rows, step 1: runs a T-SQL write batch (DECLARE, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE, IF, TRY/CATCH, THROW, its own BEGIN TRAN/COMMIT) inside a transaction that is always rolled back, and return rowsAffected per statement, any SELECT recordsets (end the batch with a verify SELECT to see the would-be state), and a previewId + approvalToken for write_apply. DISABLED unless SQLSERVER_WRITE_ENABLED=true; only environments in SQLSERVER_WRITABLE_ENVIRONMENTS, never prod or uat. Refuses DDL, EXEC, USE, GO, cross-catalog names, and ROLLBACK except `ROLLBACK; THROW;` closing a CATCH block.

database.description: Catalog to run against. Defaults to the catalog named by the connection string.

environment.description: Configured environment name. Defaults to the configured default environment.

maxRows.description: Row cap per returned recordset. Surplus rows are discarded, not cancelled.

sql.description: One T-SQL batch. No GO, no USE — `database` names the catalog.
